title: Influence and first-level Fourier weight
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ have mean zero under the uniform distribution on the cube. For each coordinate, define its influence as the uniform average of the square of the discrete derivative of $f$, and let the total influence be the sum of these coordinate influences. For each subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let its Fourier weight be the square of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$, and let the level-one Fourier weight be the sum of these weights over all singleton subsets. Then $2-\mathrm{total\ influence}(f)\le \mathrm{level\text{-}one\ Fourier\ weight}(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: The uniform mean of $f$ is zero
